shared_findings: The pre-patch local OpenAI-compatible adapter allowed arbitrary nested backend fields inside tool_calls and usage to cross the durable observation boundary; the merged adapter now projects those structures onto an explicit bounded contract.

The default urllib opener retained environment/system proxy discovery. No actual loopback proxy exfiltration was proven; the accepted refinement is to remove that ambient configuration dependency with an explicit empty ProxyHandler.
Default Python JSON accepts non-finite constants that RFC 8259 does not; the merged boundary now rejects them and cannot emit them from canonical request encoding.
Merged SHA 07f9af41ca3f4b7add75d198bebf92887c3b52d3 executed on digital-retina with 20/20 deep-integrity gates PASS and 0 FAIL.
Response projection measured over 2000 Ubuntu iterations at p50 1469 ns and p95 2651 ns for the adversarial test object; this is micro-measurement evidence, not full inference latency.

The current VPS remains an Ubuntu integration lane rather than a configured real-Qwen-4B performance lane: the separate capability receipt reports no visible GPU/runtime and real_model_executed=false.
anti_conflations: microsecond projection timing != end-to-end model latency

frank.message: Treat strict response projection as current tested infrastructure. Preserve engine-neutral OpenAI-compatible transport but admit only explicit visible/tool/usage/metric fields. Keep F6 and whole-v0.1 release false until pinned real local-model and Andreas-Ubuntu receipts exist.

harness.message: Tool calls returned by the model remain proposals/data. Route them through the external capability/effect authority and keep response-contract negative tests in the main Ubuntu integrity lane.

unifieddb.message: Persist projected model observations with provenance rather than raw provider payloads. Keep backend timing measurements and semantic tool/effect state distinct.

claygraph.message: Derive graph nodes/activation from admitted projected model observations only; unknown backend extension fields must not silently create graph truth or identity.

claycode.message: Useful typed boundary pattern: raw observation -> projected observation -> proposed effect -> authorized effect -> outcome receipt. Do not promote any BASE package from this FRANK Python implementation alone.

gwt.message: Global availability/broadcast of a model tool proposal is not execution authority. Retain distinct effect/outcome/reentry receipts and provider/runtime provenance.

hyperposition.message: Keep backend/runtime alternatives set-valued until matched real-model trials discriminate semantics, latency, memory, tool correctness and recovery. Interface compatibility alone does not collapse alternatives.

emergenz.message: Response sanitization, recurrence improvements, WAL integrity and routing success are infrastructure/functional evidence only; none establishes emergence or phenomenal consciousness.

clayresearch.message: Highest-information next model experiment is a pinned real Qwen-class 4B trial on a capable Ubuntu host through the hardened adapter, with matched prompts/templates/sampling, tool semantics, TTFT, tokens/s, memory, recurrence, rollback and provenance receipts.

next_tests: Run pinned real Qwen-class 4B tool and non-tool acceptance cases on a capable Ubuntu host through the hardened adapter.
Scale response-contract benchmarks across large tool-call arrays and argument sizes; add streaming-response contract only if FRANK enables streaming.
Run the model capability probe and final acceptance matrix on Andreas' Ubuntu developer system.
Compare supported llama.cpp/vLLM/SGLang-compatible backends under matched model/template/sampling when the execution lane exists.
Preserve separate response observation, tool proposal, effect authorization, outcome and recovery receipts in later Harness/ClayCode integration.
